summary.oneLiner: A clean turnaround quarter: net profit +17% YoY to INR 378 cr, record NII of INR 1,025 cr (+23% YoY) and NIM clawed back +28 bps QoQ to 3.23% as high-cost/bulk deposits repriced down 40-60 bps and bulk deposits were halved. Asset quality is now pristine (GNPA 1.38%, NNPA 0.26%, credit cost just 9 bps) and capital is ample (CAR 19.6%). The key overhang is governance/continuity — this is CEO P.R. Seshadri's **last call** after ~2 yrs 9 mths (second consecutive MD to exit in ~3 years), with no successor named, so he declined to bind guidance.

one-line thesis: A clean turnaround quarter: net profit +17% YoY to INR 378 cr, record NII of INR 1,025 cr (+23% YoY) and NIM clawed back +28 bps QoQ to 3.23% as high-cost/bulk deposits repriced down 40-60 bps and bulk deposits were halved. Asset quality is now pristine (GNPA 1.38%, NNPA 0.26%, credit cost just 9 bps) and capital is ample (CAR 19.6%). The key overhang is governance/continuity — this is CEO P.R. Seshadri's last call after ~2 yrs 9 mths (second consecutive MD to exit in ~3 years), with no successor named, so he declined to bind guidance.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Fee/other income soft (core fee INR 179 cr vs INR 191 cr QoQ) — management calls it a one-off (a product-renewal fee-config oversight to be fixed + weak treasury/PSLC/FX vs a strong base-year Q1). PCR incl. w/o 94.51%; excl. w/o 81.40%.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: NIM: no number given (CEO transition); believes bank is "reasonably well positioned," NIMs should harden if the rate cycle turns up (T+1 repo repricing works in the bank's favour); the sharp repricing benefit won't repeat at the same quantum.
Opex growth: ~5-6% for FY27; not expected to materially alter P&L structure; targets full-year positive operating leverage (not achieved this quarter).
Slippage: FY27 INR 500-750 cr, max INR 800 cr even assuming West-Asia deterioration.
Recoveries: FY27 INR 800-1,000 cr ("close to ~INR 1,000 cr for the year").
Credit cost: 9 bps this qtr described as "on the generous side" — expects to moderate from here.
ROA: guided 100-110/115 bps, to migrate to 120-125 bps over time.
Corporate book: wind down toward ~30% of loans long-run (from ~40%).
Trade & FX platform: go-live end-September 2026 (full capability: FX, LCs, guarantees, export/import bills).
order book & pipeline: (Bank — loan pipeline.) Gold loans +43% YoY to INR 24,930 cr (avg LTV 65.25%, avg ticket INR 2.94 lakh) though only +0.8% QoQ after ~INR 270 cr runoff of co-lending/portfolio-buy books (RBI gold circular effective 1-Apr) — underlying branch-origination growth "solid," expects material gold growth ahead. Mortgage +34%, home +19%, auto +34% YoY. MSME/business loans INR 14,391 cr (+18% ex INR 554 cr charge-off) — growth "muted" vs plan on West-Asia caution, guided back to "scale mode." FCNR-B +6% QoQ, robust, offer open to 30-Sep; upside capped by no GIFT-City entity / no external leverage lines (working on foreign-bank lines — would "materially change" volumes if secured). ECLGS: limit INR 400 cr, disbursed INR 238 cr, utilised ~INR 50 cr.
segment / subsidiary detail: Single bank entity. Asset-mix strategy: shrink corporate (opportunistically grown to ~40% on attractive short-duration corporate pricing + T-bill-linked yields) and grow better-yielding retail/MSME. Cost of deposits fell on (a) 40-60 bps downward repricing of high-rate deposits Jan-Jun, (b) average CASA balances +19%, (c) bulk deposits halved (removing overfunding/arbitrage drag). Security receipts run down INR 119 cr → INR 72 cr (INR 47 cr recovered; no fresh P&L upside — recognised at SR inception). DICGC insurance repricing benefit ~INR 10 cr QoQ (~15% for full year). Actuarial contribution back to normal at INR 84 cr (vs Q4 write-back of INR 80 cr).
growth verticals / optionality: Trade & FX platform (end-Sep go-live): FX/LC/guarantee/trade-bill revenue currently small but growing 40-50% YoY — a fee-income optionality lever.
FCNR-B / NRI franchise via Dubai rep office (scaling within UAE regulatory limits); external leverage lines pending = latent upside.
Branch re-expansion in "very key locations" after a ~3-year freeze — disciplined, revenue-accretive rollout.
Rising risk-density asset mix (retail/MSME with higher capital charge) to deploy the excess CAR and lift spreads.
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 3.23% (+28 bps QoQ, +20 bps YoY). Deposit-cost tailwind now "largely baked in" — no repeat of this quarter's sharp drop expected. Asset yields helped by mix shift + T-bill-linked corporate book in a rising-rate window. Opex to grow ~5-6%; positive operating leverage is a full-year (not Q1) target. Fee weakness flagged as fixable/one-off.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Branch rollout restarting "in a very small way" in key locations after freezing/cutting for ~3 years — deliberately paced so revenue follows expense quickly. Trade & FX systems build (end-Sep). No large physical capex.
capital allocation: CAR 19.62% / Tier-1 18.93% — ample. Excess-capital plan: grow balance sheet at system +2% and shift mix toward higher-capital-charge (retail/MSME) assets so capital gets deployed and spreads improve; ROA to migrate toward 120-125 bps. No buyback/special-dividend discussion. CEO declined firmer ROE guidance to avoid binding successor.
risks & watch-items: Leadership continuity: MD & CEO Seshadri departing after ~2 yrs 9 mths — second MD to exit in ~3 years; no successor named on call. Guidance deliberately soft as a result.
Deposit-repricing tailwind spent: NII growth from here relies on volume + any upward rate cycle, not further cost drops.
Corporate concentration ~40% vs 30% target — opportunistic, short-duration, but a mix-risk to unwind.
West Asia / Persian Gulf uncertainty: flagged for MSME caution, slippage assumptions and FCNR/NRI flows.
Fee income softness — reliant on management's "one-off/fixable" framing proving out.
Gold-loan QoQ near-flat after regulatory-driven co-lending runoff.
management quality / tone: Candid, granular and self-critical (openly admitted the fee-config oversight and that MSME growth missed plan). Numbers-rich, credible turnaround narrative (GNPA 3.15%→1.38% over the tenure). Notably restrained on forward guidance given the CEO's exit — repeatedly declined to "bind my successor," which is honest but leaves a visibility gap.
non-obvious takeaways: The headline NIM jump is a deposit-repricing event, not a structural step-up — management explicitly says the sharp reduction "is quite unlikely" to repeat; watch NII sustainability (CFO flagged the same).
Corporate book growth to ~40% is a defensive, opportunistic move (low-risk, well-priced short-duration paper amid uncertainty), not a strategy shift — reversible "practically at will."
FCNR-B upside is structurally capped by the absence of a GIFT-City entity and external credit lines — a concrete, addressable constraint worth tracking.
Governance/continuity, not fundamentals, is the swing factor into FY27 — a strong quarter handed over mid-transition.

qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): PAT INR 378 cr (+17% YoY); NII record INR 1,025 cr (+23%); NIM 3.23% (+28 bps QoQ); GNPA 1.38% / NNPA 0.26%; credit cost 9 bps; CAR 19.62%. Deposit repricing (-40/-60 bps) + bulk cut 50% drove NIM. Corporate ~40% of book (vs 30% target). Gold +43% YoY but +0.8% QoQ (RBI-circular co-lending runoff). Fee income soft (called one-off). CEO P.R. Seshadri's last call — succession open. Guidance: opex +5-6%, slippage INR 500-800 cr, recoveries ~INR 1,000 cr, ROA→120-125 bps, growth = system +2%, Trade/FX platform live end-Sep.

Q2 FY27 → check: NII/NIM sustainability once repricing tailwind fades; new MD & CEO named + any guidance reset; corporate-book wind-down toward 30%; fee-income recovery; FCNR-B flows (Aug-Sep peak) & external-line progress; Trade & FX go-live; MSME back to "scale mode."
